{{Short description|Type of topological space}}
{{for|another use|Dyadic space (cell biology)}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''dyadic compactum''' is a [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[topological space]] that is the [[continuous function (topology)|continuous]] [[image (mathematics)|image]] of a product of [[discrete two-point space]]s,<ref name="Efimov2001a">{{eom|id=Dyadic_compactum|title=Dyadic compactum|first=B.A.|last= Efimov}}</ref> and a '''dyadic space''' is a topological space with a [[Compactification (mathematics)|compactification]] which is a dyadic compactum.<ref name="Efimov2001b">{{eom|id=Dyadic_space|title=Dyadic space|first=B.A.|last= Efimov}}</ref> However, many authors use the term ''dyadic space'' with the same meaning as ''dyadic compactum'' above.<ref>{{cite book | authorlink=Ryszard Engelking | last=Engelking | first=Ryszard | page = 231 | title=General Topology | publisher=PWN | location=Warsaw | year=1977 | zbl=0373.54002 | series=Monografie Matematyczne | volume=60 }}</ref><ref> [[Teodor Przymusinski|T. C. Przymusinski]], Products of normal spaces, Ch. XVIII In K. Kunen and J.E. Vaughan (eds) ''Handbook of Set-Theoretic Topology''.  North-Holland, Amsterdam, 1984, p. 794.</ref><ref name="Hart2003">{{cite book|title=Encyclopedia of General Topology|first1=Klaas Pieter|last1=Hart|author-link1=Klaas Pieter Hart|first2=Jun-iti|last2=Nagata|author-link2=Jun-iti Nagata|first3=Jerry E.|last3=Vaughan|pages=13,193|publisher=[[Elsevier Science]]|isbn=978-0444503558|date=2003}}</ref>

Dyadic compacta and spaces satisfy the [[Countable chain condition|Suslin condition]], and were introduced by Russian mathematician [[Pavel Alexandrov]].<ref name="Efimov2001a"/> [[Polyadic space]]s are generalisation of dyadic spaces.<ref name="Hart2003" />
